# stm32flash

**Flash STM32 microcontrollers over their built-in serial bootloader**

- **Version recorded:** 0.7
- **Categories:** `programmer`
- **Upstream:** <https://sourceforge.net/projects/stm32flash/>

## What it does

Reads, writes, erases and verifies the flash of an STM32 microcontroller through the ROM bootloader ST builds into every part, over a serial line (a USB-serial adapter or a Raspberry Pi's UART) or I2C. It can also start the program it has just written, and on boards that wire them it can use the adapter's RTS and DTR lines, or GPIO, to put the chip into bootloader mode and reset it.

## Why you would want it

Many small STM32 boards have no USB bootloader and no debug header fitted, and the serial bootloader is the one way in that every STM32 has. Ham hotspot boards built on the MMDVM design are a common example (the gap analysis's search result; not measured here). It is the alternative to ST's own STM32CubeProgrammer, and complements the catalog's `stlink-tools` (an ST-LINK probe over SWD) and `dfu-util` (parts with a USB DFU bootloader).

## Before it will work

A serial connection to the board's bootloader pins (TX, RX and ground at 3.3 V logic), and access to the serial device -- the `dialout` group. The chip must be in its system bootloader: BOOT0 held high at reset, by a jumper, a button or the adapter's control lines.

## Install and launch

- **Installed with the profile:** [`electronics`](../profiles/electronics.md).
- **Install:** `hammunition install stm32flash --dry-run`, read the plan, then run it without `--dry-run`.
- **Launch:** Its package ships its own commands and application-menu entry; a unit that ships none gets a generated terminal entry (**D-050**). `hammunition status` lists what is installed.
- **The install needs the network to:** your distribution's package archive.

## Offline use

*Not yet documented for this application.* Read “Before it will work” above for what it needs; the install-time network line above is the only offline fact generated from the manifest. Internet, a local network and a radio link are three different things, and this page does not claim any of them works until it says so.

## How it installs

- apt: `stm32flash`

## Known problems

Unmeasured here: no board has been flashed with it. The commonest failure is a chip not in bootloader mode, which reports as a timeout rather than an error that says so. Some parts ship with read-out protection set; clearing it erases the chip. Getting the wrong serial device writes nothing but wastes time, so name the adapter by its /dev/serial/by-id/ path.

## Keeping it current

- probe: apt policy
- strategy: apt_upgrade
- Tagged releases are years apart (v0.7 is the latest tag); the default branch keeps adding newer STM32 parts between them. A part missing from 0.7's table is a reason to look at the upstream head, not a fault.
